title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 365
paragraphs: The inhabitants of the region also told me that this lake had an underground outlet to the Syrtis in Libya, turning toward the interior of the continent on the western side and running along the mountain above Memphis. Since I did not see anywhere the earth dug out from this excavation — a matter that caught my attention — I asked those living nearest the lake where the excavated earth had been taken. They told me where it had been carried off, and I readily believed them, for I knew by report that a similar thing had been done at Nineveh, the city of the Assyrians. There, certain thieves had once devised a plan to carry off the wealth of Sardanapallos son of Ninos, the king — wealth that was very great and kept in underground treasure-houses. They began from their own dwelling, and estimating their direction they dug underground toward the king's palace; and the earth brought out from the excavation they used to carry away, when night came on, to the river Tigris which flows past the city of Nineveh, until at last they accomplished what they desired. In the same way, as I heard, the digging of the lake in Egypt was carried out — except that it was done not by night but by day; for as they dug, the Egyptians carried to the Nile the earth they excavated, and the river, receiving it, naturally bore it away and dispersed it. This is how the lake is said to have been dug.
